rule_metadata.rule_name_english: Advanced Madd: Madd al-Farq and Aqwa al-Mudud (Madd Hierarchy)
rule_metadata.description: Comprehensive rules covering the rare 6-count distinguishing Madd (Madd al-Farq) and the precedence hierarchy when multiple secondary Madd causes overlap.

madd_al_farq.name: Madd al-Farq (The Distinguishing Madd)
madd_al_farq.definition: A rare specialized Madd found in only 4 places in the Quran. It occurs when an interrogative Hamzah (أَ) precedes a definite noun starting with the definite article Alif-Lam (الْـ).
madd_al_farq.purpose: To clearly distinguish (Farq) between an interrogative question ('Is it X?') and a mere statement of fact.
madd_al_farq.ruling: Mandatory extension of **6 counts** (acting like Madd Lazim).
locations_in_quran: آللَّهُ خَيْرٌ أَمْ مَا يُشْرِكُونَ (Surah An-Naml, v. 59)
آلذَّكَرَيْنِ حَرَّمَ أَمِ الْأُنْثَيَيْنِ (Surah Al-An'am, v. 143 & 144)

aqwa_al_mudud.name: Aqwa al-Mudud (The Hierarchy of Strength Among Madds)
aqwa_al_mudud.definition: When two different causes for lengthening apply to the same Madd letter, the stronger rule overrides the weaker one.
hierarchy_order_strongest_to_weakest: 1. Madd Lazim (6 counts) — Strongest because both sukoon and length are permanent.
2. Madd Muttasil (4-5 counts) — Strong because the Hamzah is in the same word.
3. Madd ‘Arid lis-Sukoon (2, 4, 6 counts) — Moderate because sukoon is temporary due to stopping.
4. Madd Munfasil (4-5 counts) — Weaker because the Hamzah is separated in the next word.
5. Madd Badal (2 counts) — Weakest because the Hamzah precedes rather than follows the Madd letter.

practical_examples.breakdown: Interrogative Hamzah meets definite Lam; Alif is stretched for 6 counts to clarify it is a question.
Madd Muttasil (4-5 counts) precedes Madd Munfasil (4-5 counts); both align in count tier.
